title: Evidence blobs and connector-owned sync positions

nodes.summary: Captured bytes use a nominal SDK BlobRef stored per instance
nodes.detail: BlobRef (sha256, size, mediaType, name) is a recognised nominal SDK type found by schema inspection through nested contracts, never inferred from similar records. Bytes live under the instance's evidence directory as blobs/<sha256>, and payloads hold references, not bytes or paths, with instance-local dedup only.
sections: Decision / Captured bytes have typed references

realised.evidence: BlobRef never appears in code by end of history; seq 156/157 PRs explicitly say 'no blobs'

nodes.summary: Blob downloads stream through the host, never into guest
nodes.detail: Acquisition gains StoreBlob, which the native interpreter streams to a temp file while hashing, returning a BlobResponse with HTTP status/headers so plugins can handle 429/503 and Retry-After; only complete downloads yield a reference, with no hidden retries and no guest-memory bytes.
sections: Decision / Acquisition streams through the host

nodes.summary: Blob reads confined to references in one captured snapshot
nodes.detail: readBlob/readBlobText are CapturedRead effects resolvable only for references reachable in the invocation's EvidenceSnapshot; missing or corrupt bytes are errors, never a provider refetch, and a known hash is not a historical-read API.
sections: Decision / Reads belong to one captured invocation

realised.evidence: No blob read operations in code

nodes.summary: Blobs complete before atomic publish; unreferenced bytes reclaimed safely
nodes.detail: Publication verifies every reference resolves to a complete blob before the atomic state replacement, and commits evidence, markers and position together. Afterwards bytes not referenced by Available payloads are reclaimed, and a host-only BlobScope protects in-flight readers and downloads across processes.

nodes.summary: CLI/MCP results attach read-only local file paths to BlobRefs
nodes.detail: At presentation the host finds BlobRefs via the checked result contract and supplies a read-only path to the captured local blob from the originating instance. Kyyn adds no PDF, OCR or conversion engine and keeps no second archive.
sections: Decision / Surface results expose files, not binary transcripts

realised.evidence: Depends on BlobRef, which was never implemented

nodes.summary: Typed connector sync positions persist atomically with evidence
nodes.detail: Stateful fetch takes a FetchContext (host startedAt instant and prior position) and returns a FetchResult with a plugin-defined Position type checked by the compiler. The host stores it in the state document beside evidence and advances it only on successful publication. Pagination/reset logic is plugin-owned and positions never feed history, citations or recipe progress.
sections: Decision / Sync positions are typed connector data

realised.evidence: PR #203 infers typed FetchContext/FetchResult from connector signatures and publishes evidence plus Dhall position atomically

nodes.summary: Positions survive source config changes; clear the instance to restart
nodes.detail: Only changed code or contract invalidates a stored position. A source configuration change continues the prior sync, and an agent explicitly clears the instance's evidence and position to start fresh, with no config-identity mechanism.
sections: Decision / Sync positions are typed connector data

realised.evidence: PR #203: 'Configuration has no new identity mechanism: agents explicitly clear an instance to restart'

nodes.summary: --restart-sync withholds the position once, retaining evidence
nodes.detail: evidence fetch --restart-sync passes Nothing once while keeping evidence for comparison; evidence clear deletes evidence and position; for stateless connectors restart is a reported no-op.
sections: Decision / Sync positions are typed connector data

realised.evidence: PR #204 implements generic --restart-sync and Calendar delta on typed positions

nodes.summary: No download-size or media-type exclusion policy for blobs
nodes.detail: BlobDownload drops maxBytes: there is no connector size limit or media-type skip policy, so a blob is either fully downloaded or the acquisition fails (truncation, cancellation, disk failure) without a usable reference.
sections: Decision / Acquisition streams through the host

realised.evidence: No StoreBlob/BlobDownload in code; PR #214 says blob storage is a later slice

nodes.summary: Store lock serialises publish and reclaim; no reader pins
nodes.detail: Completeness check, state replacement and reclamation run under the instance store lock, with reclamation checking current published references. BlobScope and cross-process reader/acquisition protection are dropped: blob lifetime assumes non-overlapping tool use, and concurrent read versus reclaim/clear is undefined.

realised.evidence: No BlobStorage or blob reclamation in code; PR #214 says blob storage is a later slice

editorial.note: String -> Text in BlobRef/BlobDownload/BlobResponse/readBlobText/FetchContext field types, following the SDK-wide packed Text transport owned by ADR 0007; no change to this lane's requirements

Swaps curation-register/acknowledgement vocabulary for recipe state following ADR 0014's redesign; the existing commitments (no retention of blobs, positions independent of recipe progress) are unchanged

notes: This lane was born at seq 151 as a docs-only design. Its two halves fared very differently. The sync-position half (0029.06) was built within a day (seq 156) and then refined twice by implementation PRs that loosened the spec: config changes no longer invalidate a position, and an explicit --restart-sync was added. The blob half (0029.01-05: BlobRef, streamed downloads, scoped reads, reclamation and surface file paths) is the bulk of the ADR and is still entirely unrealised; no blob identifier ever reached code, and the position PRs explicitly defer blobs. The seq 155 String->Text sweep touches this lane only as a format follow-on, so I recorded it as editorial. Seq 164 (PR #212, docs-only) simplified the unbuilt blob half before any of it was implemented: 0029.09 drops the maxBytes download policy (refines 0029.02), and 0029.10 swaps the host-only BlobScope cross-process lifetime for a store lock around publish/reclaim plus an explicit non-overlapping-use assumption (refines 0029.04). 0029.10 was judged a refine rather than a replace because complete-before-publication and reclamation of unreferenced bytes carry on; only the reader-protection part is withdrawn, which a reviewer may prefer to read as a replacement. This matches ADR 0014's treatment of the same step (0014.61). PR #214 at seq 166 lists 0029 as governing but implements only payload availability (ADR 0014) and explicitly defers blob storage, so no 0029 node is realised there.
